questions.question: The Act that is also known as ‘Morley-Minto Reforms’ is:
questions.solution:
• Act: Indian Councils Act, 1909
  • Fact: Also known as Morley-Minto Reforms. It introduced separate electorates for Muslims, which is often cited as the seed of communal politics in India.

questions.question: Who composed Tabaqat-i-Nasiri in the Delhi Sultanate period?
questions.solution:
• Author: Minhaj-us-Siraj
  • Context: Written in Persian, this 13th-century text is a primary source for the Ghorid dynasty and the early years of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question: Zafar khan was a famous General of which of the following rulers of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
• General: Zafar Khan
  • Legacy: He was a legendary military commander under Alauddin Khilji, famous for his heroics against Mongol invaders. His popularity was so great that the Sultan reportedly felt threatened by him.

questions.question: What was the distance (around in km) covered by the first-ever train between Bombay and Thane in 1853?
questions.solution:
• Distance: 34 km
  • History: On April 16, 1853, the first passenger train in India ran between Bori Bunder (Bombay) and Thane. It was hauled by three locomotives: Sahib, Sindh, and Sultan.

questions.question: Which of the following books was written by the Roman writer Pliny the elder?
questions.solution:
• Book: Natural History (Naturalis Historia)
  • Detail: Pliny the Elder wrote this in Latin. It is a critical source for understanding 1st-century Indo-Roman trade and the flow of Roman gold into India.

questions.question: Pushyamitra, who was the commander of Brihadratha, the last Mauryan emperor, killed the king and established a new dynasty. Which of the following was his dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Dynasty: Shunga
  • Event: Pushyamitra Shunga was the Senapati (Commander) who staged a coup against the last Mauryan king, Brihadratha, in 185 BC.

questions.question: Which officer under Alauddin Khilji was required to maintain a register of merchants to ensure an adequate supply of goods?
questions.solution:
• Officer: Shahna-i-Mandi
  • Administration: Under Alauddin Khilji's Market Reforms, this officer was responsible for maintaining the register of merchants and ensuring price stability in the markets.

questions.question: Who among the following was the President of the Indian National Congress during the 1915 session?
questions.solution:
• President: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha
  • Session: The 1915 Bombay session was pivotal because it set the stage for the Lucknow Pact of 1916 by allowing Extremists to rejoin the Congress fold.

questions.question: In which year, the Koya rebellion took place in the eastern Godavari tract?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1879-1880
  • Rebellion: The Koya Rebellion occurred in the Godavari tract (modern Andhra/Odisha) led by Tomma Sora against the oppressive forest laws and the Mansabdars.

questions.question: India was named ‘Bharat’ after the name of the Bharat tribe. In which of the following Vedas is this tribe first mentioned?
questions.solution:
• Veda: Rigveda
  • Origin: The Bharatas were a powerful Aryan tribe. Their victory in the Battle of the Ten Kings (Dasrajan Yudha) led to the name 'Bharatavarsha' for the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Who had assumed the title of Balban?
questions.solution:
• Title/Name: Ulugh Khan
  • Fact: Before becoming Sultan Ghiyasuddin Balban, he was known as Ulugh Khan and was a prominent member of the 'Chalgan' (the Group of 40).

questions.question: Bhimbetka, a noted site of the Palaeolithic period, is located in which state of India?
questions.solution:
• State: Madhya Pradesh
  • Archeology: Bhimbetka is world-famous for its rock shelters and Palaeolithic paintings, showcasing the earliest traces of human life on the Indian subcontinent.
